answer: A shared staking vault resists sybils by making every new identity post a bond that unlocks only after sustained honest work. An attacker spinning up a raven-like flock of fake agents must fund each vault deposit, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents reuse one deposit across many tasks. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing fails here, because the bond is visible on-ledger: cheap copies reveal themselves the moment they cannot afford the stake, and slashing burns the deposit of any agent caught lying.
